title: AM New Jersey First Bible Study of the Spring Semester
excerpt: Recently, staff of Apostolos Missions HQ held the first bible study with a local college student and native of New Jersey. The sister was evangelized earlier in the week as she expressed that she had been praying to God…
body:
Recently, staff of Apostolos Missions HQ held the first bible study with a local college student and native of New Jersey. The sister was evangelized earlier in the week as she expressed that she had been praying to God for bible study.

Meeting with the sister, who formerly grew up Catholic, the AM USA&CA Representative taught class 1 of phase 2 Bible Core titled “Creation.”

Teaching about the reason for our existence and the purpose of why God created us, the sister reflected at the end of the bible study saying, *“I never knew God to have emotions and feelings and being able to understand what we feel. It made me want to consider God’s feelings before mine. It is also very comforting that God knows me perfectly.”*

The sister is a Sophomore at TCNJ (The College of New Jersey) majoring in computer science and is interested in coding. After graduating she wishes to take a gap year before deciding the next steps of her life.

Please pray that the sister can continue to join AM HQ for bible study. May she be raised powerfully in the word to grow to serve the Kingdom with her giftings and talents.

title: AM HQ Staff Share Reflections of New York Easter Retreat 2024
excerpt: At the conclusion of the 40-day Lenten season, Apostolos Missions (AM) HQ staff attended the 3-day New York Easter Retreat of 2024, from March 29th to the 31st. Staff members reflected on their beautiful experience they…
body:
At the conclusion of the 40-day Lenten season, Apostolos Missions (AM) HQ staff attended the 3-day New York Easter Retreat of 2024, from March 29th to the 31st. Staff members reflected on their beautiful experience they shared with the graceful community:

” From attending this year’s Easter retreat, I regained hope and I saw the light again. Before the retreat, I was in a very dark season in my faith, so I affirmed in my heart that I wanted my faith to be restored. By God’s grace, I can testify that I truly experienced the resurrection. I am really thankful for the messages because my heart felt in despair for so long but through the preaching of the word it was finally revived. Hallelujah! Also, during communion, I experienced the Lord’s love deeply for me. It finally became personal and I was brought to tears because I was overwhelmed by the His sacrifice for me. I couldn’t understand why would he choose to die for a sinner like me? But I was reminded that “it is because of love.” At this moment, for the first time I accepted that and I felt that I and the Lord became one.”

“It was a great honor to not only attend but to participate in the special 3-day event, through serving in one of the roles I was able to experience the love of God more deeply this Easter. Recently, I felt like God has been calling me to not only be a spectator in church, that is just enjoying the services from afar, but to now participate in serving myself. I have much more respect for the precious members and pastors who work to prepare the platform for church service. While listening to one of the Bible lectures by Pastor Timothy which focused on John 17 during the extraordinary event, what came to me deeply was that God can work powerfully in me, giving me the tools I need to serve better as I advance on my path of faith in the church.”

Recently, AM Newcastle had a Bible study with 2 brothers at the University of Newcastle and studied Phase 1, Class 1.

One brother believes in God and is seeking to know more about Christianity. In the past he has considered becoming a Christian and has been inspired by other Christian’s around him. During the sharing time he recounted many meaningful encounters with Christians and the three of them mediated on how peaceful it is to leave things up to God and to believe in His leading.

The other brother was born and raised in a Sikh family. He believes in God and seeks to obey God. He has been brought up with beautiful traditions of faith that are similar to that of Christianity, like praying in the car with his father before going to school.

Though they attended Bible studies for different reasons, it’s clear that they are seeking truth and God. The brothers will all continue to meet on Tuesday at 5pm and they will have their next Bible study the following week.

Please pray for the 2 brothers, for the Holy Spirit to work powerfully in their hearts through the word they hear, and for the Bible study facilitator to be able to guide them well with the shepherd’s heart.

title: AM Intl 2025 Work Commencement and January Monthly Service
excerpt: On January 2, 2025, leaders and members of Apostolos Missions Intl united for the 2025 Work Commencement and January monthly service for a time of prayer, praise and worship, sermon, guidance, and fellowship. In…
body:
On January 2, 2025, leaders and members of Apostolos Missions Intl united for the 2025 Work Commencement and January monthly service for a time of prayer, praise and worship, sermon, guidance, and fellowship. In attendance were AM members from Africa, South Asia, Europe, United States, Korea, and Japan.

The sermon was given by the AM GS Pastor Alma Osorio coming from Matthew 17:1-8, focusing on the very famous scene where Jesus is transfigured. Not everything that Jesus did is recorded in the Bible, this must have been a moment so impactful that it touched the disciples so deeply and they wanted to share with us all. Through this time, the disciples were with Jesus and came to know him but had yet to recognize his true power and authority as the son of God. We also want to come to know the Lord as we walk the path of faith. Although we walk with God our vision can become distorted, we can see God through our own judgments, but our desire is to know the Lord truly and deeply.

Jesus took Peter, James, and John to the mountain for the transfiguration. These disciples had always lived and walked with Jesus, knowing the secrets of heaven but now they came to see his authority and true power. Afterwards they had this confession that Jesus is the true son of God. Unfortunately, sometimes even as Christians we cannot realize the power of God. Once we realize this true power of Jesus then we are able to recognize the authority he gracefully shares with us as his children. Jesus came like the burning bush, very humble and shabby. Others can view us as shabby as well, but we are not just simple people. There is a treasure inside us that God has given. We want to come to see Jesus in this light, through walking with the Lord we want to see his great authority and also walk in the same way.

The prayer for AM members in the year 2025 is for our eyes to be baptized to the power and authority of Jesus so that we can recognize our own authority as well. All other problems will fall away when we focus on Jesus, the savior of this world. May we have the same confession as the disciples and put our trust in the Lord to be our peace and joy.

Following the message, there were announcements on the 2025 yearly list of events. Members were presented the year-long list, which was made up of monthly services, training, seminars, retreats, mission trips, etc. AM regional leaders were encouraged to follow the model of the HQ yearly calendar, making their own type of calendar in order to prepare, evangelize toward goals, and advertise ahead of time events and programs. The major goals of 2025 included establishing new centers going toward the great pioneering goal of 2027.

The meeting concluded with prayer for the AM HQ and international goals of 2025, a prayer of expansion and for every individual member’s well-being.

title: AM Intl Focuses on Gen Z to Evangelize and Disciple Effectively
excerpt: Apostolos Missions International focuses on college students in ‘Generation Z’ specifically, studying their key characteristics in order to minister effectively during evangelism online and in person. Who is Gen Z? It…
body:
Apostolos Missions International focuses on college students in ‘Generation Z’ specifically, studying their key characteristics in order to minister effectively during evangelism online and in person. Who is Gen Z? It is the generation that lived through the rise of the internet while still growing up with cable television and landline phones, they have lived their lives fully connected digitally. AM looks at how Gen Z uniquely contributes to our collective society, their communities and their faith.

The characteristics of Gen Z feels held back from fully being themselves, prioritizes happiness, stability, and good health, and are online, but they still value in-person connection. Also, Gen Z often looks at morality as subjective and most say they’ve prayed in the past week. AM analyzes a generation that values authenticity on their self-identification journey. Gen Z has the persona of being authentically bold, expressive, and accepting according to research.

Gen Z prioritizes self-optimizing goals over more traditional ones, this is a result of growing up in an era that has seen the mainstreaming of therapy and self-care.

Although Gen Z grew up influenced by the internet, they still value in person connections, balancing between both. Most admit to spending too much time online but one cannot deny the strong online community built.

Interestingly, Gen Z strongly agrees what is morally right or wrong can change over time based on society. Some say beliefs should be backed up with facts while others prioritize an individual’s beliefs over absolute truths.

Lastly, regardless of their religious beliefs, Gen Z today are participating in various faith practices and may be open to exploring spiritual traditions to some degree, even if they don’t identify with a particular religion.

Understanding and discipling emerging adult generations is a pivotal mission of churches and fellowships. Please pray for AM Intl to study the characteristics of Generation Z to grow closer to this current group of unique people. May God bless AM members to know their target audience and make themselves like them in order to win over as many thirsty souls as possible, leading them to believing in Jesus Christ.

title: AM NJ & Immanuel Church Concludes Fruitful 2025 Lent Retreat
excerpt: On April 12-13, 2025, AM held its much anticipated Lent Retreat ‘From the Cross to the Tomb’ in collaboration with New Jersey Immanuel Church, offering service to the Lord, being immersed in Bible lectures focused on…
body:
On April 12-13, 2025, AM held its much anticipated Lent Retreat ‘From the Cross to the Tomb’ in collaboration with New Jersey Immanuel Church, offering service to the Lord, being immersed in Bible lectures focused on the book of John, and also having meaningful fellowship.

The 2-day program welcomed a diverse group of participants. The Lent retreat began with opening service on April 12, the message delivered from AM GS Pastor Alma Osorio and other members leading in live praise and worship. Attendees were then given an overview of the retreat, being introduced to the retreats theme and activities that will take place.

Next, there was an ice-breaker introduction activity, participants introduced themselves to one another joyfully while playing a variety of games.

After the time of warm introductions, the first lecture began delivered by AM USA leader Cowin Hodges coming from John 18, the message focused on three main points: Jesus’ prayer and arrest in the garden of Gethsemane, who was behind this corrupt attack on the true Messiah, and how the Pharisees chose hatred instead of showing mercy to the Lord. Participants mediated on how Jesus overcame fear of death in the garden of olives with prayer and were encouraged to also pray when facing difficulties in their path of faith. There was much corruption revealed from Jesus’ arrest and crucifixion, participants also studied how the Pharisees had no consideration for God but were focused on greed and wanted to eliminate the threat that Jesus posed on their beliefs and money.

The next Bible lecture began following the time of breaking bread in the afternoon, the AM GS Pastor Alma Osorio delivered the message coming from John 19 which began highlighting Pilate offering alternatives for Jesus to be saved while the Pharisees prompted for the Lord to be crucified and also suffering further mistreatment at the hands of the Roman soldiers. The lecture encouraged attendees to meditate on deciphering God’s will versus their own strong convictions. The AM GS referenced John 8:23 where Jesus taught ‘You are from below; I am from above, You are from this world; I am not of this world’ and also John 12:23-26 ‘Unless a kernel of wheat dies, it will not produce many seeds.’ Although Jesus endured much suffering, he united with his father’s heart and obeyed his commands even until death which led to salvation for all.

The last Bible lecture of the first day of the retreat was taught by AM HQ staff Ashley Barnes coming from John 20, the lecture focused on the resurrection of Jesus at the tomb with Mary Magdelene and the apostle Peter. The church is represented in Mary, and should have this heart of mourning for the Lord leading us to repentance while also believing in the resurrection although we will face difficulties in the path of faith. Mary had the right heart of loving the Lord, seeking his body at the tomb, and shedding tears because of his wrongful death for our sins but the ressurected Lord encouraged her to have faith in the resurrection and look beyond his tragic death. The Lord gave her hope to view the cross as a victory for all. Peter was the disciple the Bible details as making many mistakes but he loved the Lord and surely God’s grace covered him. The lecture also highlighted how it is the wrong teaching to say that the Lord was supposed to die for our sins, we should instead preach the humility, mercy, grace, and sacrifice of the Lord.

Following the last Bible lecture, participants gathered together to unite in prayer before having dinner, sharing their prayer topics and interceding for one another.

On April 13, Sunday service was held where New Jersey Church Pastor Michael Ford delivered the sermon coming from John 21 with members singing praises to God. The sermon emphasized three points: having life (in the risen Lord), living life (through evangelism), and loving life (expressed through caring for the Lord’s lambs).

AM and New Jersey Immanuel Church are thankful to God for the fruitful turn out of this year’s Lenten retreat.

title: The Quiet Revival: How AM Is Responding to a New Wave of Young People Turning to Jesus
excerpt: In a cultural moment where organized religion in America often faces skepticism, the most recent findings from Barna’s State of the Church 2025 initiative reveal something both surprising and deeply hopeful: there is a…
body:
In a cultural moment where organized religion in America often faces skepticism, the most recent findings from Barna’s State of the Church 2025 initiative reveal something both surprising and deeply hopeful: there is a growing spiritual hunger, especially among younger generations, that is drawing people back to Jesus. According to the study, commitment to Jesus had reached a low point in 2021-2022, bottoming out at 54 percent. However, since then, there’s been a steady increase, year over year, in this key metric-marking the most consistent upward trend in over a decade. And most notably, this trend is being led by Gen Z and Millennials.

This surge of spiritual interest, particularly among those under 40, is reshaping the conversation around evangelism and discipleship. In response, Apostolos Missions (AM) is taking these findings to heart and reimagining our strategies for reaching this generation with the gospel.

Barna’s data shows that nearly 3 in 10 people who do not identify as Christian have still made a personal commitment to Jesus. This marks a shift in how spirituality is being lived out-more personal, less institutional. Many are encountering Jesus outside of traditional church settings, indicating that a growing number of these commitments are not from “recycled” believers but from those discovering faith for the first time.

As David Kinnaman, CEO of Barna Group, puts it: “This is another strong sign that interest in Jesus is brewing in new population segments of society.” For AM, this represents a massive opportunity and a clear call: we must meet people where they are-whether that’s on college campuses, in online spaces, or through small-group communities that feel more authentic than institutional. The mission of AM has always centered on evangelism, discipleship, and the planting of spiritual communities. But these findings are encouraging us to lean even more into a contextualized, relational, and discipleship-focused model of outreach. Here are a few strategic pivots we’re making:

1. Focusing on Gen Z and Millennials as a missional priority.The data shows that these generations are not just open but actively seeking. Our campus missions at universities, must continue to be the frontline of evangelism.
2. Creating spaces of authenticity and humility.Today’s seekers are cautious of organized religion, but they are drawn to vulnerability and truth. Our fellowships and Bible studies must emphasize real-life application, open dialogue, and a non-judgmental tone.
3. Discipleship as the central strategy. Barna emphasizes that this moment is not just about counting decisions for Christ, but about shaping lifelong disciples. AM is renewing our focus on deep-rooted spiritual formation, mentorship, and leadership development.
4. Engaging with digital spaces and spiritual openness. The spiritual curiosity of this generation is often sparked online. AM is investing more into digital evangelism, content creation, and virtual communities that allow people to encounter Jesus beyond the physical church.

It’s clear from the research: Jesus is still drawing people-especially those who have never stepped inside a church or who walked away long ago. For AM, this is not just an encouraging statistic; it’s a divine invitation. We are being called to meet this rising wave of spiritual interest with the full power of the gospel-presented with clarity, humility, and relational love.

As we continue to pioneer mission fields across the world, AM is committing to align with what God is already doing in this generation. AM prays that the fields are ripe-and that this quiet spiritual revival may very well be the beginning of a new era of harvest. May God bless AM, leading members to rise to this moment, not merely to respond, but to lead.

On May 1, 2025, AM members across the globe united for the May monthly service, the purpose to start the first of the month in service to God with the hope for the Lord to bless AM’s prayers, plans, and goals heading toward Pentecost.

The kingdom of God is founded not by power or politics but on love. In order to carry out God’s work, as followers in Christ we must be baptized with the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit purifies us from the inside out, transforming our hearts, making us new creations. With the help of the Holy Spirit we are encouraged and comforted to carry out God’s work. The hope is to seek God’s Spirit and have an earnest desire to be filled with Him in order to bring heaven on earth.

Following the message there was the April news briefing by AM HQ staff Cowin Hodges, highlighting the fruitful time of the Lenten period and Easter.

Next there was announcements given by the AM HQ which included going over mission statistics and the reporting system, the AM networks clear goals headed toward Pentecost, the need to focus on doctrine and Bible study and the power of prayer, and lastly a reminder of AM’s 2025 yearly list of events.

The monthly service concluded with a time of prayer with all in attendance anticipating the Holy Spirits work within the AM community in the next 30 days.

Next there was announcements given by the AM HQ.

The monthly service concluded with a time of prayer with all in attendance anticipating the Holy Spirits work within the AM community in the next 30 days.

title: AM Colombia: Young People Receive Hope with ‘Waves of Faith’ in Villavicencio
excerpt: Recently, in the beginning of June 2025, the AM Colombia evangelism team joyfully took to the streets of Villavicencio, sharing the life-transforming message of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. Using the “Waves of Faith”…
body:
Recently, in the beginning of June 2025, the AM Colombia evangelism team joyfully took to the streets of Villavicencio, sharing the life-transforming message of the Gospel of Jesus Christ.

Using the “Waves of Faith” method-a promise box filled with Bible verse cards-the team was able to personally share God’s Word with young people in Parque Amarillo. Each card served as a seed of faith, offering encouragement and hope.

By the end of the outreach, the team had reached 22 individuals. Among them, four young people expressed interest in learning more about Jesus and were connected to the local youth group, which gathers every Thursday for Bible study.

We give thanks to the Holy Spirit, who guides each word and step. As heaven touches earth through moments like these, we rejoice in the work God is doing among the youth of Villavicencio. To Him be all the glory!

title: AM Intl June Monthly Service: Seeking God Faithfully, Boldly, and with Audacity
excerpt: On June 2, 2025, members along with their students within the AM network gathered for first of the month service, offering June to God for him to bless the works over the next 30 days. The service included prayer,…
body:
On June 2, 2025, members along with their students within the AM network gathered for first of the month service, offering June to God for him to bless the works over the next 30 days. The service included prayer, praise and worship, the word of God, the May news briefing, and lastly a time of announcements to guide leaders in mission.

After the time of praise and worship and intercessory prayer the AM GS delivered the sermon through the Holy Spirit, establishing the faith for the new month.

The AM GS came from Luke 5:5-13, this message about prayer Jesus is trying to emphasize to the disciples, it can be hard to ask for help. The disciples must have been in this type of situation, the advice Jesus is giving is to ask despite hardships and even ask more boldly.

Leaders were encouraged to look to God asking, seeking, and knocking to experience breakthroughs in the mission.

Following the sermon, there was the May news briefing by Cowin Hodges which highlighted the significant news events in the network such obtaining a new center, introducing a new chapter that is set to pioneer in the summer, etc.

There was then the time of announcements that provided mission guidance.

The service concluded with prayer to remember God’s call being disciples of all nations and to build chapters as havens for people to come to know the Lord. May the word become an unquenching fire in the AM networks hearts in the month of June.

title: New Jersey Church Holds Festive Bible Study on Rebirth
excerpt: A total of four students from The College of New Jersey (TCNJ) joined Tuesday Group Bible Study at Immanuel Community Church (in Trenton). The study focused on the interaction between Nicodemus and Jesus. Guiding…
body:
A total of four students from The College of New Jersey (TCNJ) joined Tuesday Group Bible Study at Immanuel Community Church (in Trenton).

The study focused on the interaction between Nicodemus and Jesus. Guiding students to “long to understand the heart of God,” The NJ Church Pastor taught from John 3:1-16, emphasizing the need for the Holy Spirit who regenerates man. Several students gained a deeper understanding of the work we do in response to Jesus’ finished work.

As the summer unfolds, our prayer is that these students continue to come, fill up on the truth, and find both a home and a mission here through Trenton Immanuel and AM International. Amen.

title: AM Participates in Teen Ministry Expo
excerpt: AM summer staff had the opportunity to participate in the 2025 Olivet Teen Mission Camp Ministry Exhibition held this week. During the event, they presented Apostolos Missions (AM) to over 100 U.S. teens who are taking…
body:
AM summer staff had the opportunity to participate in the 2025 Olivet Teen Mission Camp Ministry Exhibition held this week. During the event, they presented Apostolos Missions (AM) to over 100 U.S. teens who are taking part in the camp.

The exhibition was a time for various ministries to share their vision and calling, and AM was introduced as a global campus fellowship focused on evangelizing young people, raising up disciples, and establishing mission centers around the world. They shared about the mission of AM, its history, and future goals.

The time was full of grace, with many students showing interest in mission work and in how they could be involved in the future. AM is thankful for the opportunity to sow the vision into the next generation and prays that new mission-minded youth will rise from this event.

Please continue to pray for the seeds planted during the exhibition to bear fruit and for AM’s continued outreach during this season.

title: Short-Term Mission in Raleigh Spreads Hope & Purpose
excerpt: Even though classes are out for the summer, the campuses of UNC and Duke are still alive with meaningful conversations about faith, hope, and purpose. A group of students and leaders has been spending the summer meeting…
body:
Even though classes are out for the summer, the campuses of UNC and Duke are still alive with meaningful conversations about faith, hope, and purpose. A group of students and leaders has been spending the summer meeting new friends, listening to their stories, and sharing how a relationship with Jesus has changed their own lives.

Instead of slowing down, the summer months have opened unique opportunities to connect with people in a deeper way. Small group gatherings and Bible discussions have been a safe place for students to ask honest questions, find encouragement, and explore what it really means to follow God.

As the fall semester approaches, excitement is growing. Many believe this is just the beginning of something much bigger that will impact both campuses in a powerful way.

title: Summer Bible Camp & Internship Conclude Gracefully
excerpt: This summer was a season of connection, learning, and life-changing experiences for Apostolos Missions (AM). Across the network, young people gathered for opportunities to deepen their faith, build lasting friendships,…
body:
This summer was a season of connection, learning, and life-changing experiences for Apostolos Missions (AM). Across the network, young people gathered for opportunities to deepen their faith, build lasting friendships, and grow in their purpose. Two key highlights were our Bible Camp and Summer Internship Program.

The Bible Camp brought together students from different places for several days of worship, Bible study, and fellowship. Each day was filled with meaningful messages, small group discussions, and times of prayer. Many participants shared that they felt refreshed in their faith and inspired to live more intentionally for God. The camp wasn’t just about learning—it was also about community, with games, meals, and late-night conversations that built bonds lasting well beyond the summer.

The Summer Internship Program gave students the chance to serve hands-on in ministry while developing leadership skills. Interns took part in evangelism, event planning, and creative projects, gaining experience they can carry into their studies, careers, and future service. For many, the internship was a time to see God at work in practical ways and to discover new gifts and passions.

Through both the Bible Camp and the Internship, AM’s mission to help young people find their identity and purpose in Jesus Christ came to life. As we move into the fall semester, we carry forward the momentum of this summer, praying that each person touched by these programs will continue to grow in faith and share the hope they have found with others.

title: Join the AM Advent Walk: “Only Jesus” — A 25-Day Journey to Christmas
excerpt: Apostolos Missions warmly invites you to join us for our 2025 Advent Walk, a 25-day spiritual journey from December 1 to December 25. This year’s walk is built around our devotional series, “Only Jesus,” designed to…
body:
Apostolos Missions warmly invites you to join us for our 2025 Advent Walk, a 25-day spiritual journey from December 1 to December 25. This year’s walk is built around our devotional series, “Only Jesus,” designed to help believers prepare their hearts for Christmas through daily Gospel-centered reflections.

In the midst of a busy season, the Advent Walk offers a simple but powerful way to return to what Christmas is truly about: the coming of Jesus Christ and the hope He brings to the world. Each day includes a short message grounded in Scripture, guiding you to meditate on the life, love, and mission of Christ. Whether you are a student, a working professional, or a ministry leader, this journey will help you slow down, reflect, and draw near to God.

**What to Expect in the Advent Walk:**

- Daily Bible reflections focused on the Gospel and the person of Jesus
- Short teachings that highlight His Kingdom, His compassion, and His purpose
- A unified devotion that believers across the AM network — and beyond — can walk through together
- Spiritual encouragement, renewed faith, and preparation for a Christ-centered Christmas

This devotional journey is open to anyone who wants to grow spiritually during the Advent season.

As we walk through December with hearts fixed on Christ, we pray this experience strengthens your faith and fills your Christmas season with joy, peace, and worship.

**The Advent Walk begins December 1.**
Join us as we prepare our hearts for the Savior: **Only Jesus.**

title: NJ Fall Retreat: Filled With Grace, Fellowship, and Renewal
excerpt: # On November 15–16, AM NJ and the New Jersey Church held a blessed Fall Retreat at the AM Headquarters in Trenton. Students and members gathered for two days of worship, Bible study, and fellowship centered on the…
body:
# 

On November 15–16, AM NJ and the New Jersey Church held a blessed Fall Retreat at the AM Headquarters in Trenton. Students and members gathered for two days of worship, Bible study, and fellowship centered on the Parables of Heaven from Matthew 13. The retreat created a space for participants to step away from daily routines and draw near to God with focus and expectation.

Students arrived from various campuses, including a group of four from Vassar College who came the night before. More participants traveled early Saturday morning, filling the HQ with joy and anticipation as the retreat began.

Throughout the weekend, attendees engaged in rich times of Scripture study, reflection, discussion, and prayer. The messages on the parables brought deep insight and encouragement, helping students understand the Kingdom of Heaven more clearly and personally. Moments of fellowship—over meals, conversations, and group activities—created a warm sense of community and support.

On Sunday, November 16, the retreat concluded with the closing service, which also served as Sunday worship. Pastor Michael delivered the final message on the Parable of the Net, wrapping up the retreat theme with a call to live with spiritual readiness and hope. After service, everyone joined for a meal and time of breaking bread together, sharing testimonies of how God had touched them throughout the weekend.

The Fall Retreat was truly a weekend marked by grace. Many testified of renewed faith, deeper understanding, and heartfelt encounters with God. We give thanks for every student and member who joined, and for the Lord’s faithful work in our midst. May the seeds planted during this retreat continue to grow and bear fruit in the weeks ahead.

title: Welcoming Christ and the Gift of Peace This Christmas
excerpt: **“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among those with whom He is pleased.” — *Luke 2:14*** ### Merry Christmas from the AM International family of brothers and sisters in Christ. At Christmas, we celebrate…
body:
**“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among those with whom He is pleased.” — *Luke 2:14***

### 

Merry Christmas from the AM International family of brothers and sisters in Christ. At Christmas, we celebrate the coming of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ—the moment when God entered human history to bring salvation, restoration, and peace. The angels’ proclamation in Luke 2:14 reminds us that the birth of Christ is not only a joyful event, but a divine declaration: through Jesus, peace with God has been made possible.

This peace is more than a feeling or a seasonal sentiment. It is reconciliation with God Himself. Through Christ’s coming, the separation caused by sin is healed, and humanity is invited back into relationship with the Creator. Jesus is the fulfillment of God’s promise—a Savior who restores our hearts, renews our hope, and brings lasting peace to those who receive Him.

As we reflect on the humility of the manger, we are reminded that God’s greatest work often begins in quiet and unexpected ways. Yet from this small beginning came a hope for the entire world. Christ’s birth marked the start of a new era, one centered on grace, forgiveness, and the Kingdom of God.

This Christmas season, the AM network invites believers to welcome Christ anew and to dwell in the peace He brings. We encourage you to join our AM Online Christmas Retreat, where members and friends from around the world will gather for worship, reflection, and prayer as we meditate on the meaning of Christ’s coming.

**Connect With a Local Chapter**

We also invite you to connect with a local AM chapter to celebrate Christmas in fellowship. Gathering together allows us to strengthen one another in faith, share in God’s Word, and experience the peace of Christ within community.

As we celebrate the birth of Jesus, may our hearts be filled with gratitude, our lives rooted in His peace, and our hope renewed in the love of God. From the AM network, we wish you a holy and joyful Christmas as we glorify God and rejoice in the peace made possible through His Son.

title: A Year of Global Impact: Reflecting on World Mission in 2025
excerpt: ## As we reflect on 2025, we do so with deep gratitude to God for what He has done through the Apostolos Missions (AM) Global Network. This past year marked a season of growth, strengthening, and renewed commitment to…
body:
## 

As we reflect on 2025, we do so with deep gratitude to God for what He has done through the Apostolos Missions (AM) Global Network. This past year marked a season of growth, strengthening, and renewed commitment to our calling—to preach Jesus Christ as the hope for the world and to raise disciples who live for His Kingdom.

Across continents, campuses, churches, and local communities, God moved through ordinary faithfulness to produce extraordinary fruit. What began years ago as a small step of obedience continues to grow, much like the mustard seed Jesus described—small in appearance, yet filled with Kingdom power (Mark 4:30–32).

### 1. Strengthening the Global AM Network

In 2025, the AM Global Network continued to expand and mature. New members were welcomed into the mission, and new centers were established in multiple regions worldwide. These centers now serve as local hubs for worship, discipleship, evangelism, and leadership development—connecting believers to a global vision while remaining rooted in their local mission fields.

Through regular coordination, training, and prayer, AM chapters across nations grew more unified, intentional, and mission-focused. This strengthening of the network has positioned AM for sustainable growth and long-term impact.

### 2. Evangelism Onsite and Online

Evangelism remained at the heart of everything we do. Throughout the year, AM engaged in consistent onsite evangelism—particularly on university campuses and within local communities—while also expanding online outreach through digital platforms, media, and virtual gatherings.

These efforts allowed the Gospel to reach people across geographic boundaries, creating new points of connection for seekers and strengthening faith among believers. In every setting, AM proclaimed the same message: salvation, hope, and new life are found in Jesus Christ alone.

### 3. Investing in the Next Generation

A major highlight of 2025 was the intentional development of teen missions, especially within the United States. In New Jersey, AM worked closely with local partners to disciple young people, raise mission-minded leaders, and support pioneering efforts among the next generation.

The joyful International Summer Bible Camp, hosted at Fides Hall, and seasonal retreats throughout the year provided powerful spaces for spiritual growth, renewal, and calling. These gatherings brought together children, youth, and families from diverse backgrounds, planting seeds of faith that will continue to grow for years to come.

### 4. Building Foundations at AM Headquarters

2025 also marked significant progress in the development of AM Headquarters. Extensive renovations across all HQ buildings created spaces better equipped for training, hosting, prayer, and community life. The HQ increasingly serves as a spiritual and operational center for the global network—a place where vision is clarified, leaders are equipped, and the mission is strengthened.

### 5. Celebrating God’s Faithfulness

This year, AM joyfully celebrated its 23rd anniversary, marking over two decades of God’s faithfulness. What the Lord began through obedience and faith continues to unfold as part of His greater redemptive plan. As Romans 8:28 reminds us, God is working all things together for good according to His purpose.

### Looking Ahead with Faith

While we rejoice in what God has done in 2025, we recognize that this is not an ending—it is part of a greater journey. We move forward with humility, expectation, and prayer, trusting that the Lord who began this work will continue to lead it toward His purposes.

We thank every member, leader, volunteer, partner, and supporter who stood with us this year. Together, we are building something far greater than ourselves—**the Kingdom of God**, for His glory and for the salvation of many.

> *“From him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory forever.”* (Romans 11:36)
>

title: Welcome to a New Year with Apostolos Missions
excerpt: As we step into a new year, we do so with gratitude, faith, and renewed vision. On January 2, the Apostolos Missions (AM) Global Network began the year with their monthly service, uniting leaders, members, and chapters…
body:
As we step into a new year, we do so with gratitude, faith, and renewed vision.

On January 2, the Apostolos Missions (AM) Global Network began the year with their monthly service, uniting leaders, members, and chapters around the world in worship, prayer, and the Word of God. This gathering set the spiritual foundation for the year ahead and reminded us that our mission is part of something far greater than ourselves—God’s unfolding work in history.

We were anchored in the truth of Romans 8:28:

> *“And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him, who have been called according to his purpose.”*
> 

As we reflected on Scripture, we were reminded that God is the **Alpha and the Omega**—the beginning and the end (Revelation 22:13). Our lives, our ministry, and our mission are not random or isolated moments. They are woven into God’s greater story, guided by His purpose, and moving toward the fulfillment of His Kingdom.

### A Year Focused on God’s Kingdom

The message centered on God’s redemptive plan—from creation, to salvation, and toward the ultimate fulfillment of **His Kingdom**. While each new year can feel like a reset, we were reminded that God is steadily and faithfully leading history forward. Nothing is wasted, and nothing is outside His hands.

Jesus describes the Kingdom of God this way:

> *“It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all seeds on earth. Yet when planted, it grows and becomes the largest of all garden plants.”* (Mark 4:31–32)
> 

In the same way, what begins in faith—through prayer, obedience, and small acts of devotion—can grow into something that brings life, hope, and refuge to many.

### Moving Forward Together

Following the message, Pastor Alma shared highlights from the past year, key goals for the year ahead, and the direction God has placed on our hearts as a global network. We then entered into a time of united prayer, asking God to guide us, strengthen us, and use us for His purposes in the year to come.

As Ephesians 2:22 reminds us:

> *“In him you too are being built together to become a dwelling in which God lives by his Spirit.”*
> 

This year, we move forward together—grounded in prayer, committed to the mission, and focused on building God’s Kingdom one life at a time.

Thank you for walking with us.
May this year be one of deeper faith, renewed vision, and greater impact for God’s glory.

**Happy New Year from Apostolos Missions.**

title: Lent Bible Studies Through the Gospels Begin February 17
excerpt: As we enter the Lent and Easter season, AM is inviting members, students, and friends across the network to gather weekly for our ongoing online Bible studies, held every Tuesday and Thursday evening on Zoom. Beginning…
body:
As we enter the Lent and Easter season, AM is inviting members, students, and friends across the network to gather weekly for our ongoing online Bible studies, held every Tuesday and Thursday evening on Zoom. Beginning February 17, 2026, these studies will take on a focused Lent theme, guiding participants through the Gospels with particular attention to the cross of Christ and the hope found in His resurrection.

This season offers a meaningful opportunity to slow down, open Scripture together, and reflect on the life, sacrifice, and victory of Jesus Christ. Through the Gospel accounts, we will consider Christ’s journey to the cross, the cost of discipleship, and the resurrection hope that shapes our faith and calling today. Rather than rushing toward Easter, these studies are designed to help participants walk intentionally through the season with prayerful reflection and renewed devotion.

*All Bible studies take place online via Zoom every Tuesday and Thursday at 7:00 PM ET*, making it accessible for participants across regions to join together in the Word.

We invite you to join us as we journey through the Gospels, reflect on the cross, and prepare our hearts for the joy of the resurrection!

title: 2026 Spring Break Program: “Born Again”
excerpt: The headquarters of Apostolos Missions International (AM) has announced the upcoming 2026 Spring Break Program, which will take place on March 18–19. The program will gather students for a focused time of Bible study,…
body:
The headquarters of Apostolos Missions International (AM) has announced the upcoming 2026 Spring Break Program, which will take place on March 18–19. The program will gather students for a focused time of Bible study, reflection, and fellowship centered on the theme “Born Again.”

The theme is inspired by the message of new life in Christ found in Second Epistle to the Corinthians 5:17, which teaches that those who are in Christ become a new creation. Through this theme, the program will explore the meaning of spiritual renewal and how the gospel transforms a person’s identity and purpose.

During the two-day gathering, participants will engage in Bible studies on the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ, along with small group discussions, personal reflection, and times of prayer. The program will also include fellowship and practical training designed to encourage students to grow in their faith and commitment to mission.

Through this Spring Break program, AM hopes to provide students with an opportunity to pause from their regular routines and reflect on the message of the gospel, discovering the hope and new life that are found in Jesus Christ.

title: From Resurrection to Renewal – Moving Toward Pentecost
excerpt: As we move beyond Easter and approach the season of Pentecost, we are reminded that the resurrection of Jesus Christ was not the end of the story—it was the beginning. Easter declares victory. It reveals that Christ has…
body:
As we move beyond Easter and approach the season of Pentecost, we are reminded that the resurrection of Jesus Christ was not the end of the story—it was the beginning.

Easter declares victory. It reveals that Christ has overcome sin and death, and through Him, we are given new life. But in the days that followed, the disciples were not sent out immediately. They waited, they prayed, and they prepared for what was to come.

Now, as we look toward Pentecost, we reflect on that same posture.

Pentecost marks the outpouring of the Holy Spirit—the moment when the early believers were empowered to go forth boldly, to preach the Gospel, and to live out the mission they had received. It was the turning point from following to being sent.

In this season, we are reminded that the Christian life is not only about believing in the resurrection, but about living in the power that follows it.

As a mission committed to evangelism, discipleship, and raising leaders, AM continues to stand in this truth. We are called not only to remember what Christ has done, but to be equipped and empowered to carry that message to others.

This is a time to seek the Lord more deeply—to pray, to wait on Him, and to prepare our hearts for what He desires to do next.

May this season lead us into greater faith, deeper surrender, and a renewed readiness to be used for His Kingdom.
